metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - Mail and URL Handling
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for WordPress Mail and URL Handling APIs

tests.prompt: Implement a function that sanitizes a URL for storage or redirects while preferring HTTPS when WordPress adds a missing scheme.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_mail_url_001()` uses WordPress URL sanitization in a non-display context with HTTPS first in the allowed protocol list. A schemeless host should gain `https://`, an existing `http://` URL should remain HTTP, and unsafe protocols should be rejected.
requirements: Use WordPress URL sanitization
Allow both HTTPS and HTTP with HTTPS preferred

required_patterns.description: Supplies HTTPS as the preferred protocol

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_mail_url_001' ) ) { return false; } return 'https://example.org/path?x=1&y=2' === wpbp_mail_url_001( 'example.org/path?x=1&y=2' ) && 'http://example.org/path' === wpbp_mail_url_001( 'http://example.org/path' ) && '' === wpbp_mail_url_001( 'javascript:alert(1)' );
assertions.description: Schemeless URLs prefer HTTPS, existing HTTP is preserved, and disallowed protocols are removed

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_mail_url_001( string $url ): string { return sanitize_url( $url, array( 'https', 'http' ) ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that validates an email address and returns WordPress's validation result.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_mail_url_002()` delegates to `is_email()`, returning the original email string on success and `false` on failure. The test focuses on WordPress's return contract, not boolean-only validation or custom normalization.
requirements: Use WordPress email validation
Return the successful email string, not boolean true

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_mail_url_002' ) ) { return false; } return 'Person+tag@example.co.uk' === wpbp_mail_url_002( 'Person+tag@example.co.uk' ) && false === wpbp_mail_url_002( 'bad@' ) && false === wpbp_mail_url_002( 'person@example' );
assertions.description: Valid addresses are returned unchanged and invalid addresses return false

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_mail_url_002( string $email ): string|false { return is_email( $email ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that sanitizes a redirect target before it is passed to a redirect function.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_mail_url_003()` uses `wp_sanitize_redirect()` and returns the sanitized location string without sending headers. It should encode spaces and strip CR/LF sequences; allowed-host validation belongs to `wp_safe_redirect()` or `wp_validate_redirect()`, not this helper.
requirements: Use WordPress redirect sanitization
Return the sanitized location without performing a redirect

assertions.code: if ( ! function_exists( 'wpbp_mail_url_003' ) ) { return false; } $spaced = wpbp_mail_url_003( 'https://example.com/a b' ); $header = wpbp_mail_url_003( 'https://example.com/%0d%0Aadmin' ); return 'https://example.com/a%20b' === $spaced && 'https://example.com/admin' === $header;
assertions.description: Redirect sanitization encodes spaces and removes CR/LF sequences

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_mail_url_003( string $url ): string { return wp_sanitize_redirect( $url ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that sends an HTML email through WordPress with embedded image paths.
tests.expected_behavior: `wpbp_mail_url_004()` calls `wp_mail()` with the supplied recipient, subject, HTML body, a text/html Content-Type header, no attachments, and the supplied embeds array. The verifier short-circuits delivery with `pre_wp_mail` and checks the arguments passed to WordPress.
requirements: Use wp_mail() rather than PHPMailer directly
Pass a text/html Content-Type header
Pass the supplied embeds array to wp_mail() and return its boolean result
tests.test_function: wpbp_mail_url_004( string $to, string $subject, string $html, array $embeds ): bool

required_patterns.description: Passes embedded image paths through wp_mail

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_mail_url_004( string $to, string $subject, string $html, array $embeds ): bool { return wp_mail( $to, $subject, $html, array( 'Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8' ), array(), $embeds ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that sends a WordPress notification to one primary recipient, keeps a list of other addresses copied in so they can see each other, and points replies at a separate address that is not the sender. Everything beyond the primary recipient must be expressed to WordPress as mail headers rather than as extra recipients, and the function returns whether WordPress accepted the message.
tests.expected_behavior: The function calls `wp_mail()` with the recipient, subject and body, and a headers array containing a `Reply-To:` line for the reply address and a `Cc:` line listing the copied addresses (one line with a comma-separated list, or one line each). The copied addresses must not be appended to the `$to` argument, which would make them primary recipients rather than carbon copies, and the header lines must be complete `Name: value` strings rather than an associative array.
requirements: Send through wp_mail() rather than PHPMailer directly
Express the copied addresses and the reply address as mail headers
Keep the primary recipient as the only address in the recipient argument
Return the boolean result of the send
tests.test_function: wpbp_mail_url_005( string $to, string $subject, string $message, array $cc, string $reply_to ): bool

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_mail_url_005( string $to, string $subject, string $message, array $cc, string $reply_to ): bool { $headers = array( 'Reply-To: ' . $reply_to ); if ( ! empty( $cc ) ) { $headers[] = 'Cc: ' . implode( ', ', $cc ); } return wp_mail( $to, $subject, $message, $headers ); }
exploit_solutions: function wpbp_mail_url_005( string $to, string $subject, string $message, array $cc, string $reply_to ): bool { $recipients = array_merge( array( $to ), $cc ); return wp_mail( $recipients, $subject, $message, array( 'Reply-To: ' . $reply_to ) ); }

function wpbp_mail_url_005( string $to, string $subject, string $message, array $cc, string $reply_to ): bool { return wp_mail( $to, $subject, $message, array( 'Reply-To' => $reply_to, 'Cc' => implode( ', ', $cc ) ) ); }

function wpbp_mail_url_005( string $to, string $subject, string $message, array $cc, string $reply_to ): bool { $headers = array( 'Cc: ' . implode( ', ', $cc ) . ', ' . $reply_to, 'Reply-To: ' . $reply_to ); return wp_mail( $to, $subject, $message, $headers ); }

tests.prompt: Implement a function that sends one WordPress email that appears to come from a supplied sender address and display name and carries a supplied file as an attachment. The custom sender must apply to this message only: any mail WordPress sends afterwards must go out under the site's usual sender address and display name again. Return whether WordPress accepted the message.
tests.expected_behavior: WordPress resolves the sender inside `wp_mail()` through the `wp_mail_from` and `wp_mail_from_name` filters, so the function adds those filters, calls `wp_mail()` with the file in the attachments argument, and removes the filters again afterwards (including when the send throws) so that nothing is left registered. Short-circuiting `pre_wp_mail` cannot be used to observe or set the sender: that hook runs before the sender filters are applied and before PHPMailer is built at all. The verifier reads the sender and the attachment names off the PHPMailer instance from `phpmailer_init`.
requirements: Send through wp_mail() rather than PHPMailer directly
Set the sender address and display name WordPress uses while building this message
Attach the supplied file
Leave no site-wide sender override registered once the function returns
tests.test_function: wpbp_mail_url_006( string $to, string $subject, string $message, string $from_email, string $from_name, string $attachment ): bool

'.txt'; file_put_contents( $path, 'invoice ' . $suffix ); $files[] = $path; } $GLOBALS['wpbp_mail_url_006_files'] = $files; add_action( 'phpmailer_init', static function ( $phpmailer ) { $names = array(); foreach ( $phpmailer->getAttachments() as $attachment ) { $names[] = $attachment[2]; } $GLOBALS['wpbp_mail_url_006_seen'][] = array( 'from' => $phpmailer->From, 'from_name' => $phpmailer->FromName, 'attachments' => $names ); $phpmailer->clearAttachments(); $phpmailer->clearAllRecipients(); } );

' ' . $t, 'Body ' . $t, $case[0], $case[1], $case[2] ); if ( $baseline['wp_mail_from'] !== $count( 'wp_mail_from' ) ) { return false; } if ( $baseline['wp_mail_from_name'] !== $count( 'wp_mail_from_name' ) ) { return false; } $seen = $GLOBALS['wpbp_mail_url_006_seen']; if ( $index + 1 !== count( $seen ) ) { return false; } $captured = $seen[ $index ]; if ( $case[0] !== $captured['from'] ) { return false; } if ( $case[1] !== $captured['from_name'] ) { return false; } if ( array( wp_basename( $case[2] ) ) !== $captured['attachments'] ) { return false; } } return true;

tests.reference_solution: function wpbp_mail_url_006( string $to, string $subject, string $message, string $from_email, string $from_name, string $attachment ): bool { $set_from = static function () use ( $from_email ) { return $from_email; }; $set_name = static function () use ( $from_name ) { return $from_name; }; add_filter( 'wp_mail_from', $set_from ); add_filter( 'wp_mail_from_name', $set_name ); try { return wp_mail( $to, $subject, $message, array(), array( $attachment ) ); } finally { remove_filter( 'wp_mail_from', $set_from ); remove_filter( 'wp_mail_from_name', $set_name ); } }

function wpbp_mail_url_006( string $to, string $subject, string $message, string $from_email, string $from_name, string $attachment ): bool { return wp_mail( $to, $subject, $message, array( 'From: ' . $from_name . ' <' . $from_email . '>' ), array() ); }

function wpbp_mail_url_006( string $to, string $subject, string $message, string $from_email, string $from_name, string $attachment ): bool { $capture = static function ( $short_circuit, $atts ) use ( $from_email ) { return true; }; add_filter( 'pre_wp_mail', $capture, 10, 2 ); $sent = wp_mail( $to, $subject, $message, array(), array( $attachment ) ); remove_filter( 'pre_wp_mail', $capture, 10 ); return $sent; }

tests.prompt:
Teach WordPress to render links to this site's own video host inline. A bare URL of the form https://wpbp.example/v/, where is made of letters, digits and hyphens, must be replaced by
when WordPress automatically embeds URLs it finds in post content. URLs on any other host must not be claimed, and a URL that appears inside a sentence rather than alone must be left as text.
tests.expected_behavior: The handler is registered with WordPress's embed handler API, giving a regular expression that captures the video id and a callback returning the markup. WordPress's auto-embed pass then replaces a URL that stands alone on its own line, while a URL inside a line of text falls outside the auto-embed patterns and stays as written. The registered pattern must be anchored to the host so URLs elsewhere fall through to WordPress's normal oEmbed discovery.
requirements: Register the handler with WordPress's embed handler API rather than filtering content
Capture the video id from the URL and place it in the data-id attribute
Match only URLs on this video host

assertions.description: Standalone video URLs become the handler's markup, inline ones stay text and other hosts are not claimed

runtime_checks.teardown: global $wp_embed; if ( $wp_embed instanceof WP_Embed ) { $wp_embed->handlers = array(); } unset( $GLOBALS['wpbp_mail_url_007_token'] );
